posts.text: A sperm whale's echolocation clicks hit 230 decibels, the loudest sound any animal makes. Close up, a diver feels it in the chest.
comments: That is a hunting tool, aimed at giant squid thousands of feet down in total darkness.

posts.text: African greys are more prone to a couple of specific conditions than smaller parrots are, and one of them is the signature illness of the species.
comments: Hypocalcemia is the one. Veterinary sources describe it as the most common cause of central nervous system disease in African greys specifically.
Watch for muscle tremors, weakness, and in serious cases seizures. It is not something to sit on.
Feather destructive behavior is the other. African greys are noted as especially prone to it compared with budgies and cockatiels.
Full list of what to watch for in this species → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/african-grey-parrot-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: A shoebill stands motionless for hours, then detonates into a strike fast enough to snap a lungfish in half.
comments: The clog-shaped bill has sharp edges built for slicing tough prey. It is not decoration.

posts.text: A thorny devil never drinks with its mouth. Grooves between its scales pull water in by capillary action and route it to the jaw.
comments: Morning dew off its own back is a full water supply. It also wears a fake spiked head on its neck as a decoy.

posts.text: Veiled chameleons are one of the cheapest ways into the species. The setup and the vet bills are where the real number lives.
comments: Captive-bred juveniles are the cheapest option, and unlike most reptiles there is barely a morph market here. Hypo and hyper melanistic mutations exist and cost more, but the selection is genuinely thin.
Two places will not let you keep one at any price. Washington DC allows only non-venomous snakes, fish and turtles, so every lizard is out, and Hawaii bars anything not on an approved list.
Check that before the sticker price, not after.
Full cost breakdown here → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/veiled-chameleon-cost-guide/

posts.text: An aye-aye taps bark up to eight times a second and listens for the hollow spot where a grub is hiding, then hooks it out with the same finger.
comments: That middle finger is thin, skeletal, and double-jointed. No other animal forages this way.

posts.text: Giant manta rays have the largest brain relative to body size of any fish, in the range you see in some mammals.
comments: In mirror tests they linger at a real mirror and blow bubbles while watching themselves. Full card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/oceans-biggest-brain/

posts.text: Guinea pigs mask illness well, which is exactly why routine care matters more here than it feels like it should when everything looks fine.
comments: Respiratory infection is the urgent one. Guinea pigs are obligate nasal breathers, so they cannot fall back on mouth breathing if the nasal passages block.
Scurvy is the species-specific one. Like us, they cannot make their own vitamin C, and deficiency weakens the immune system, slows wound healing, and disrupts bone and tooth development.
Almost entirely preventable with the right diet, which is the useful part.
Everything worth being able to recognize → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/guinea-pig-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: A cornered horned lizard ruptures blood vessels near its eyes and fires a stream of blood several feet at a coyote.
comments: It is loaded with chemicals from the ants it eats that canines find repulsive. Against birds it barely works, so the whole trick is aimed at dogs.

posts.text: An echidna has no teeth. It flicks a sticky tongue in and out up to 100 times a minute and grinds ants with hard pads in its mouth.
comments: Its snout also reads the faint electrical signals of prey underground, a sense usually reserved for animals that hunt in water.

posts.text: The koi is usually the smallest number in the whole equation. Koi ownership is pond ownership, and the pond is where the budget lives.
comments: Juvenile pond-quality domestic koi run $10 to $100, often $10 to $50 for a small 4 to 6 inch fish. Better colored specimens run $45 to $200 or more.
Imported Japanese koi average roughly $100 to $1,500, and show quality goes well past that.
Bloodline, body conformation, pattern clarity and size drive it. Kohaku, Sanke and Showa varieties command real premiums over domestic mixed colors.
Full breakdown, pond included → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/koi-cost-guide/

posts.text: A mudskipper can leave the water and stay out in open air for hours, breathing through its skin and the lining of its mouth.
comments: Cutaneous respiration covers up to 60 percent of its oxygen on land. It props itself on its front fins like arms.

posts.text: A Draco lizard's ribs extend into wings. It glides up to 60 meters between trees without flapping anything.
comments: Ribs, repurposed as an airframe. Card here → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-flying-dragon/

posts.text: Western hognoses are hardy, and nearly everything that goes wrong traces to substrate, humidity, or feeding, all fully inside an owner's control.
comments: Respiratory infection is the common one. Open-mouth breathing, wheezing, drooling or visible mucus, and lethargy.
It comes from humidity running too high, so the fix starts with the enclosure rather than the snake.
A digital thermometer and hygrometer is the single best tool for catching it early, because it lets you confirm the numbers instead of guessing at them.
Full list and the numbers to hold → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/hognose-snake-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Some nudibranchs eat stinging jellyfish and keep the stinging cells instead of digesting them, then redeploy them as their own defense.
comments: The cells pass intact through the gut and out into projections on the slug's back. Nobody is fully sure how it avoids firing them on the way.

posts.text: Tardigrades make a protein called Dsup that coats their DNA and shields it from radiation.
comments: Put the Dsup gene into cultured human cells and radiation damage dropped by about 40 percent in a 2016 study.

posts.text: Degus are cheap individually, and the whole budgeting point is that individually is not how you should be thinking about this purchase.
comments: An individual degu runs $10 to $50, with adoption at the lower end. But this species is obligately social, so plan on at least a same-sex pair from day one.
A large multi-level cage is most of the total on its own, alongside a solid wheel, bedding, hides, and a sand bath.
Add the pair on top of the equipment figure, not the other way around.
Full cost picture → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/degu-cost-guide/

posts.text: A sea otter packs up to a million hairs into a single square inch, the densest fur on earth.
comments: It has no blubber, so that fur is the only insulation, which is why grooming eats hours of its day.

posts.text: Platypuses have no nipples. Mothers sweat milk through patches of skin on the belly and it pools in grooves for the babies to lap up.
comments: One of several things that fall out of being a mammal that also lays eggs. Card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/milk-without-nipples/

posts.text: Praying mantises are one of the cheapest exotic pets going, to buy and to keep, with one caveat about how long you will actually have one.
comments: Carolina and Chinese mantises run $15 to $35. Ghost mantises $15 to $75 depending on age. Orchid mantises, the showpiece, can reach $150.
Most species stay well under $75 even so.
Buy an adult or subadult, not a nymph. Nymphs are genuinely hard to keep through their many molts, and a failed molt is usually fatal.
Full costs and the lifespan caveat → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/praying-mantis-cost-guide/

posts.text: The female king cobra is the only snake known to build a nest, dragging leaves into a waterproof mound nearly a meter tall.
comments: She lays inside it and stays close to guard until they hatch.

posts.text: A frilled-necked lizard snaps open a huge collar of skin, hisses, and gapes a brightly colored mouth. If the bluff fails it sprints off on its back legs.
comments: Tail out for balance, running upright. All threat display, no follow-through.

posts.text: A cockatoo is a financial and emotional commitment that plays out over decades. The purchase price is the smallest part of it.
comments: Umbrella cockatoos commonly run $1,000 to $3,000. Moluccans around $1,400 to $3,500. Rarer species like the palm cockatoo go higher still.
Adoption is worth serious consideration here. Rescue fees run $300 to $800.
That gap exists because cockatoos are one of the most commonly surrendered large parrots, which is the part of the story the price tag does not tell.
Full breakdown before anyone commits to this one → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/cockatoo-cost-guide/

posts.text: A toco toucan's bill is more than a third of its body surface, and it works as a radiator.
comments: By adjusting blood flow it can dump up to four times its resting heat production through the bill, then shut that down to keep warm.

posts.text: A southern cassowary's inner toe carries a dagger claw over 4 inches long, capable of lethal wounds if the bird feels cornered.
comments: Despite the reputation they are shy fruit eaters that would much rather disappear into the forest. Card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-dagger-toe/

posts.text: Corn snakes are one of the hardier pet snakes, and nearly every health problem they develop traces back to husbandry rather than bad luck.
comments: Respiratory infection is the most common issue, usually bacterial and almost always secondary to an enclosure that is too cold or too damp.
It needs a reptile vet and prescription antibiotics, not a wait-and-see. Left alone it gets serious quickly.
Get temperature and humidity right and most of the rest of the list never shows up.
Full list of what to watch for → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/corn-snake-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: The kakapo is the only flightless parrot alive and the heaviest, with males up to 4 kg. It is also nocturnal, which parrots generally are not.
comments: In breeding season males boom a call that carries for miles.

posts.text: A male satin bowerbird builds a twig avenue purely to impress, then decorates it with blue objects stolen from rival bowers.
comments: It is not a nest. Nothing is raised there. Females just prefer the bluer one.

posts.text: Most serious bearded dragon health problems trace back to husbandry, not bad luck. Which is good news, because it means most of the list is preventable.
comments: Metabolic bone disease is the most common serious illness in pet beardies, and almost always preventable. Calcium deficiency, or inadequate or incorrect UVB.
If you see the signs, vet promptly, and in the meantime handle gently and take the climbing furniture out.
A dragon with weakened bones can fracture something in a fall that would not normally hurt it at all.
Full list, and when it is time to call → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/bearded-dragon-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Dumbo octopuses flap two ear-like fins to move, and live deeper than any other known octopus, one confirmed at nearly 7,000 meters.
comments: That is the hadal zone. Crushing pressure, near freezing, and a small octopus flapping through it.

posts.text: The vampire squid does not drink blood. It eats marine snow drifting down through the oxygen-poor twilight zone.
comments: Threatened, it flips its webbed arms inside out over itself like an umbrella and shows spines instead of running. Card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/not-a-vampire-at-all/

posts.text: Oscars are cheap to buy and expensive to house properly. The tank and the filtration, not the fish, are where the budget goes.
comments: Juvenile tiger and standard oscars run $7 to $35, clustering low for 1 to 2 inch fish. Specialty color and finnage varieties often pass $100.
An aquarium retailer's line about lifespan says more than any price tag: this fish can live as long as a dog.
Between the personality and a decade-plus lifespan, it is closer to a pet than to a fish you keep.
Full cost picture → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/oscar-fish-cost-guide/

posts.text: A leafy sea dragon's leaf-shaped flaps do nothing for swimming. They are pure camouflage.
comments: It moves on nearly invisible fins on its neck and back, so from a distance it reads as drifting seaweed.

posts.text: Lionfish carry eighteen venomous spines. First spotted off Florida in 1985, likely released from home aquariums.
comments: They are now one of the most damaging invasive species in the Atlantic.

posts.text: Jumping spiders, the regal especially, are one of the most affordable and least space-hungry pets on the whole site.
comments: Captive-bred spiderlings run $15 to $25. Juvenile or sub-adult females run $25 to $60, and they are generally more prized than males because they live considerably longer.
Named regional color forms cost more than standard animals.
Prices last checked September 2026 at Josh's Frogs and Dubia.com. Treat any number like that as a snapshot, not a quote.
Full breakdown → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/jumping-spider-cost-guide/

posts.text: A pangolin's tongue is anchored back near its pelvis and stretches longer than its own head and body combined.
comments: No teeth at all. The tongue does the entire job, thousands of ants at a time.

posts.text: A cheetah goes 0 to 60 in about three seconds, then has 20 to 30 seconds before it overheats.
comments: Its claws never fully retract, which is unusual for a cat and works like cleats mid-sprint. Card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/zero-to-sixty-in-seconds/

posts.text: Rats are hardy for their size, but one condition affects nearly all of them to some degree, and recognizing it matters more here than with most small pets.
comments: The Merck Veterinary Manual calls chronic respiratory disease, caused by Mycoplasma pulmonis, the most common health problem in rats. It is not rare or unlucky.
There is no cure. Antibiotics ease a flare-up, and that is the extent of it.
Merck is direct about the outlook: rats with the chronic form rarely live longer than 2 years. That single fact is why housing quality matters so much in this species.
Full list and what housing actually changes → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/rat-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that fly backwards, and they can hover briefly upside down, on a shoulder joint that rotates a full circle.
comments: At night they drop into torpor and cut their heart rate by up to 95 percent.

posts.text: Aardvark teeth have no enamel and no roots, keep growing for life, and are built from bundles of tiny hexagonal tubes.
comments: It is the only living species in its entire mammalian order. Nothing else is close.

posts.text: Uromastyx sit near other popular pet lizards on price, but the setup runs higher than average, because of how hot and specialized the enclosure has to be.
comments: Common captive-bred species, Mali and ornate among them, sit in the usual range, hatchlings low and adults higher. Rarer or imported species reach $300 to $800.
Color drives price here more than anything else. Bright reds, oranges, greens and blues cost more than the common drab brown or grey animals.
As a rule, the more colorful the uromastyx, the more it costs.
Full cost breakdown, enclosure included → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/uromastyx-cost-guide/

posts.text: The green anaconda is the heaviest snake alive but not the longest. Reticulated pythons beat it past seven meters.
comments: The anaconda is built on a different scale of thickness and can pass 100 kilograms where a python of the same length does not.

posts.text: An owl's flight is almost silent. Comb-like serrations on the leading feather edge break up turbulence and a velvety surface muffles the rest.
comments: The prey never hears it coming. That is the entire design.

posts.text: Leopard geckos are generally hardy, but one of the conditions on this list has no cure at all, which makes early recognition genuinely load-bearing.
comments: Metabolic bone disease is common in this species partly because they are so often kept without UVB, without proper calcium supplementation, or without a regulated heat source.
All three of those are setup decisions, made before the animal ever shows a symptom.
Which is the useful framing: most of this list is husbandry with a delay on it.
Full list and the warning signs → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/leopard-gecko-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: A flamingo can sleep standing on one leg because it locks the joint, so holding the pose costs no muscle effort at all.
comments: Researchers think the habit conserves body heat while wading in cold water. Card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-one-leg-trick/

posts.text: A giraffe's neck holds exactly seven vertebrae, the same count as yours, just enormously stretched.
comments: Wild giraffes also barely sleep. One tracking study logged as little as 10 minutes a night, in a couple of short bursts.

posts.text: Gerbils are one of the more affordable small pets, with the same caveat as degus. You are budgeting for two animals, not one.
comments: Most gerbils run $10 to $20 at a pet store, and adoption often lands at $10 or less, sometimes with a starter cage thrown in.
This species has to be kept in same-sex pairs or small groups, so plan for at least two from the start.
The cage is the real line item, same as it is with every small pet on this site.
Full cost picture → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/gerbil-cost-guide/

posts.text: A box turtle's lower shell hinges shut, sealing it inside almost completely.
comments: They also have a strong sense of home. Move one far from its territory and it may spend years trying to get back, which is why you never relocate one.

posts.text: Boa constrictors do not suffocate prey. Constriction cuts blood flow so fast that blood pressure crashes and the animal faints within seconds.
comments: Biologist Scott Boback's team measured it. The suffocation story was wrong. Card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/not-a-suffocation-squeeze/

posts.text: Angelfish are hardy in a properly sized, well-maintained tank. Most health problems trace back to water quality and stress rather than to the fish.
comments: Ich reads as small white spots like grains of salt, plus flashing against decor, clamped fins, and rapid gill movement.
It gets triggered by stress and by sudden temperature changes or declining water quality, which is the same root cause behind most of the list.
Fix the water first. It is almost always the answer and it is almost never the first thing people reach for.
Full list of what shows up → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/angelfish-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: An elephant seal dives past 2,000 meters and holds its breath for up to two hours.
comments: It collapses its own lungs and drops its heart to a few beats per minute to do it.

posts.text: Bats are the only mammals capable of true sustained flight, and many navigate pitch darkness by firing up to 200 calls a second.
comments: They read the echoes into a live map of the room. Not a rough sense of direction, a map.

posts.text: Argentine tegus are one of the more expensive lizards to set up properly, and it is a direct consequence of how large this species gets.
comments: Standard black and white tegus, plus blue and Chacoan morphs, run $200 to $500. Designer morphs, albino and high white among them, go $700 to $1,200 or more.
The animal is not the problem. The adult enclosure is.
This is a lizard that grows into furniture, and the budget has to be built around that rather than around the hatchling in front of you.
Full cost breakdown → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/argentine-tegu-cost-guide/

posts.text: An alligator burns through 2,000 to 3,000 teeth in a lifetime. Every one of its 80 teeth has a replacement already growing underneath.
comments: The moment one wears down or snaps, the next pushes it out.

posts.text: Quokkas look permanently delighted because of the shape of the mouth, which is how they got called the world's happiest animal.
comments: They are small wallabies, and mothers can pause a pregnancy mid-development when food runs short, then restart it. Card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-worlds-happiest-selfie/

posts.text: Birds hide illness because prey animals do. By the time a budgie looks visibly sick it is often further along than a mammal would be at the same point.
comments: The single biggest preventable problem is the all-seed diet. Seeds are calorie dense and nutritionally incomplete.
Over time that drives obesity and hepatic lipidosis, a fatty liver condition serious enough to cause sudden death.
Finding an avian vet before you need one is the other half of it. That is not a thing you want to be searching for at 9pm.
Full list of what to watch for → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/budgie-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Meerkat mobs post a lookout on a raised mound and swap the shift roughly every hour so everyone gets to forage.
comments: They are also partly immune to scorpion venom, so they can eat the scorpion that would drop most other animals.

posts.text: Red foxes pouncing on prey hidden under snow strongly favor jumping toward magnetic northeast, and their kill rate on that heading is far better.
comments: They also hold the largest natural range of any wild carnivore on earth.

posts.text: Nearly everything on the crested gecko health list traces back to three things: calcium, humidity, and substrate. Get those right and most of it never appears.
comments: Metabolic bone disease comes from a deficiency in calcium or vitamin D3, and it is progressive, which is exactly why catching it early matters.
Progressive means the window closes quietly rather than slamming.
None of these are exotic problems. They are setup decisions showing their results months later.
Full list → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/crested-gecko-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: For decades the immortal jellyfish was filed under the wrong name, including in the 1996 paper that made it famous.
comments: A 2026 study confirmed Turritopsis nutricula is a separate Atlantic lineage that cannot reverse its life cycle at all.

posts.text: Researchers played 17 female dolphins the signature whistles of 11 males. Fertile females swam away from the whistles of the aggressive herders.
comments: They were tracking individual males by reputation, across the population. Card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/names-on-a-watchlist/

posts.text: With hedgehogs the first real decision is not financial or even husbandry. It is legal, and that is an unusual thing to have to lead with.
comments: Six places will not let you keep one: California, Georgia, Hawaii, Pennsylvania, Washington DC and New York City. New Jersey has its own requirements on top.
Check that before you fall in love with a specific hedgehog, not after.
Once that is settled they are moderately priced to buy and genuinely inexpensive month to month.
Full cost and legal picture → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/hedgehog-cost-guide/

posts.text: In a marine heatwave 4C above average, researchers measured 134 clownfish getting shorter. Not thinner, shorter, reabsorbing their own tissue.
comments: Around three quarters of the dominant fish shrank at least once, and a single shrinking event raised survival odds by 78 percent.

posts.text: Lions are the only social cat out of roughly forty species, and the pride is built on related females who often stay for life.
comments: Males are not part of that lineage. They arrive as a coalition, hold it two or three years, then get pushed out by a stronger one.

posts.text: Tokay gecko prices have a huge range, and that range is really a quality divide rather than a market one.
comments: Wild-caught or unspecified normals run as low as $15 to $50, and they are genuinely not recommended, given the parasite load and the temperament typical of wild-caught animals.
Captive-bred normals start around $100 and go up from there.
This is one of the few species where the cheap option is the actively worse one rather than just the plainer one.
Full cost breakdown → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/tokay-gecko-cost-guide/

posts.text: A crocodile is more closely related to a sparrow than to a monitor lizard. Crocodilians are archosaurs, the group that contains dinosaurs and birds.
comments: The resemblance to lizards is body plan, not ancestry. Card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/closer-to-birds-than-lizards/

posts.text: Around 5,500 tigers remain in the wild across thirteen countries. A century ago the estimate was near 100,000.
comments: They have lost 93 to 95 percent of their historic range, and the Bali, Caspian and Javan tigers are already gone.

posts.text: Nearly everything on the guppy health list connects back to one root cause. Guppies are hardy, and stressed, poorly maintained water opens the door to all of it.
comments: Ich shows as small white spots like grains of salt across the body and fins, along with flashing against decor, rapid breathing, and lethargy.
The trigger is stress, usually from temperature swings or declining water quality.
Which means the first move on almost any guppy problem is the same one: test the water before you treat the fish.
Full list → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/guppy-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: A rhino horn has no bone in it at all. It is compacted keratin the whole way through, the same protein as your fingernails.
comments: Structurally it is closer to an enormous callus than to a cow's horn, which is bone in a keratin sheath.

posts.text: A three-toed sloth climbs all the way down to the forest floor about once a week to defecate, then climbs back.
comments: On the ground it cannot walk, it drags itself by the front claws. Roughly half of sloth predation deaths happen on those trips. Card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-weekly-trip-that-kills-them/

posts.text: Green cheek conures sit at a moderate price for a parrot, and two things push that number up fast: color mutations and the wrong sales channel.
comments: Normal green conures run $250 to $500 from breeders for hand raised, weaned babies, with common listings around $275 to $400.
Common morphs, Pineapple, Yellow-Sided, Cinnamon and Turquoise, run higher.
Where you buy matters as much as what you buy, which is true of most parrots and rarely discussed in the listing.
Full cost picture → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/conure-cost-guide/

posts.text: A fennec fox's ears run about 15 centimeters on an animal under two kilograms, the largest ears relative to body size of any carnivore.
comments: They are full of shallow blood vessels, so the fox dumps heat straight out through them.

posts.text: The Victoria crowned pigeon is about 75 centimeters long and up to 2.5 kilograms. A pigeon you would notice from across a field.
comments: Blue-grey, maroon breast, deep red eye, and a fan of lace crest standing straight up.

posts.text: Milk snakes are hardy, and most of what goes wrong comes down to enclosure moisture and temperature. Both are fully inside an owner's control.
comments: Wheezing, nasal or oral discharge, and open-mouth breathing all point to respiratory infection.
The causes are temperatures running too cool, humidity that is off, or poor ventilation.
Three numbers, held steadily, prevent most of this list. That is genuinely the whole job with this species.
Full list and the numbers → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/milk-snake-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: An orangutan's arm span reaches 7 feet, wider than the animal is tall, and it spends over 95 percent of its life in the canopy.
comments: Largest tree-dwelling animal on earth, on shoulder and hip joints that rotate more freely than yours.

posts.text: A border collie named Chaser learned the names of 1,022 different toys and could pull the right one out of a pile on command.
comments: She could also work out a brand new toy's name by noticing it was the only thing in the group she did not recognize. Card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/a-thousand-word-vocabulary/

posts.text: Emperor scorpions are one of the cheaper exotics to buy and to keep. The scary invertebrate reputation does not come with a scary price tag.
comments: Captive-bred specimens typically run $25 to $100, with juveniles at the lower end.
Three jurisdictions ban the animal outright, and that is worth settling before any money changes hands.
It is a recurring theme across the exotics on this site. The legal question comes before the financial one more often than people expect.
Full cost and legal breakdown → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/emperor-scorpion-cost-guide/

posts.text: The shima enaga is a real wild bird, a Hokkaido-only long-tailed tit that ends up with a completely white face as an adult.
comments: In winter it fluffs up for insulation until it looks like a snowball with a tail.

posts.text: The okapi is the giraffe's only living relative, zebra stripes notwithstanding. Its tongue runs 14 to 18 inches, long enough to clean its own eyes.
comments: It lives only in the rainforests of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

posts.text: Two problems account for the vast majority of pacman frog health issues, and both are tied directly to how the animal is fed and housed.
comments: Obesity is the first. Pacman frogs are in a real sense programmed to eat whenever the opportunity shows up, and they do not self-regulate the way some pets do.
That makes portion control an owner's job rather than the frog's.
It is one of the most common issues keepers run into, and it is entirely a husbandry decision.
Full list → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/pacman-frog-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: The pygmy marmoset weighs about as much as a stick of butter and fits in a palm. Smallest monkey in the world.
comments: It lives largely on tree sap, gouging holes in bark and coming back to the same trees to drink what runs out.

posts.text: Orca pods are led by the oldest female, and her sons and daughters stay with her for life.
comments: Each pod has its own dialect of clicks and whistles that calves spend years learning, and those traditions hold for decades. Card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/killer-whale-family-trees/

posts.text: Discus are one of the pricier community fish to keep, and the cost is not the fish. It is the filtration and the water-change routine the species demands.
comments: Young common-strain discus run $20 to $40. Nicer adults more typically $50 to $150.
Premium or rare strains, blue diamond, pigeon blood, high-grade red melon, regularly climb past $200.
None of those numbers are the reason discus are expensive to keep, which is the part worth understanding before buying one.
Full cost picture → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/discus-cost-guide/

posts.text: Atlantic puffins return to the exact same burrow year after year, often to the same partner for 15 to 20 years, after spending most of the year apart at sea.
comments: When they find each other again they tap bills and preen before settling in to raise a single chick.
